Subject: Dedicated pool warmup fallback: impact, short-term mitigation, and next steps (Acme Retail)

Hi Sophie / John,

Thanks again for your patience this morning. I wanted to confirm what happened and what we did to get your reserved pool back to normal. We know this impacted burst/low-latency calls for a subset of your services and we’re treating this as a priority.

Summary (short):
- Incident start: 2029-08-12 07:22:33 PDT (us-west-2 dedicated pool for Acme Retail)
- Impact: increased tail latency and ~15-25% request failures for ~48 minutes; no data exposure
- Root cause (short): a warmup ‘storm’ combined with an autoscaler probe regression and a routing flag that prevented automatic fallback to compatible model variants
- Status: service restored at 08:10 PDT after we manually re-enabled fallback and applied a temporary autoscaler threshold patch

What we did (immediate):
- Rolled back routing flag "allow_fallback=false" that had been toggled in the 2029.07.31 rollout for a config optimization. That flag prevented our runtime from routing traffic to lower-cost but compatible variants during warmup.
- Applied a temporary autoscaler probe threshold increase to avoid oscillatory scaling while node warmup persists.
- Drained a small set of nodes that experienced preemption failures and replaced them.

Attachments: acme_incident_timeline.pdf (high-level timeline) and routing_policy_snapshot.txt (config snapshot at time of incident).

Immediate next steps we are executing:
1) Formal RCA and postmortem (target: 72 hours)
2) Credit proposal for measurable impact window (we will send a preliminary offer within 24 hours)
3) Technical remediation: rework flag rollout gating, autoscaler probe hardening, and a canary for fallback behavior

I’ve looped in our on-call ops and platform leads (Ben, Karthik, Grace) — they will follow up with a technical deep-dive and an ETA for the full remediation.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll prioritize clarity and concrete actions; you should expect the timeline PDF and a support ticket (INC-2029-4782) to show up in your inbox.

Best,
Camila
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Camila / team — quick tech note from the ops deep-dive (early findings):

1) Warmup storm: when the scheduled rolling maintenance (control plane upgrade) returned nodes to ready state, a backlog of cold KV-cache priming requests from Acme’s tail traffic created sustained CPU/PCIe contention on a subset of GPUs. That activity caused longer-than-expected warmup (KV/cache misses and model weight pageloads).

2) Autoscaler probe regression: a change in the probe health-check timeout (released in 2029.07.31) made the autoscaler treat partially-warmed nodes as unhealthy and repeatedly triggered scale-down/start-up cycles while a subset of requests were still completing initialization. The oscillation amplified the warmup window.

3) Fallback routing disabled: the routing flag "allow_fallback=false" (intent: reduce cross-variant routing during peak) prevented automatic redirects to compatible model variants (e.g., small-llama-7b from large-llama-13b). In prior incidents fallback reduced tail-failures; here it would have materially reduced impact.

What we pulled as artifacts (attached as stubs): kv-cache-log-snippet.txt (KV cache thrash and pageload timestamps), routing_policy_snapshot.txt (flag present), autoscaler-events.log (internal reference).

Short-term action taken (already done): re-enabled fallback, bumped probe timeout to 45s, manually stabilized the pool and stopped the oscillation. That matched the service restoration at ~08:10 PDT.

Notes for RCA: we need to look at combined blast radius of config flags vs autoscaler tuning. Separately, we should check why canary gating for the routing flag didn’t prevent cross-tenant exposure (flag rollout used a config group that included both hosted and dedicated pools).

Ben
Director, Platform Reliability

Team — proposed remediation and owners:

1) Short term (week):
   - Harden autoscaler probe logic (owner: infra-engineering) — change: add two-step readiness check to avoid scale oscillation; ETA: 2029-08-16
   - Restrict routing flag rollout groups and add explicit tenant isolation (owner: runtime-config) — ETA: 2029-08-18
   - Add an early-warning KV cache metric to the console (owner: telemetry) — ETA: 2029-08-20
2) Long term (quarter):
   - Implement safe-fallback canary: fallback behavior will be progressively enabled with traffic-splitting and safety gates (owner: serving runtime) — target: 2029-10-01
   - Autoscaler simulation harness to reproduce warmup oscillations offline (owner: reliability research) — target: 2029-10-15
3) Customer-facing commitments:
   - Postmortem and full RCA: 72 hours from incident (target: 2029-08-15 14:00Z)
   - Preliminary credit proposal: 24 hours (we will email Sophie by 2029-08-13 EOD)
Notes: we should coordinate messaging to customers about rolling maintenance windows to avoid surprises. Also propose a short-runbook update listing client-side retry/backoff best practices to limit downstream amplification.

KL
VP, Platform Engineering

Following the internal deep-dive, here’s the agreed customer-facing plan and the deliverables you can expect from Redwood:

1) RCA / Postmortem: we’ll publish a detailed RCA by 2029-08-15 14:00Z (link to Drive: https://drive.redwood.example/shared/acme-postmortem-20290812). That doc will include the timeline, root causes, and telemetry excerpts.

2) Remediation timeline (customer-impact items):

   - Config rollout gating for fallback flags — will be restricted and audited by 2029-08-18
   - Early-warning metrics and dashboard tile for KV/cache warmup (console) — 2029-08-20
3) Credits: preliminary credit proposal sent (separately) — we calculate the impacted window as 2029-08-12T14:22:30Z to 2029-08-12T15:10:00Z. We will apply a service credit that maps to the percentage of failed calls during this window; expect a formal offer by 2029-08-13 EOD and a billing adjustment within your next invoice cycle.
4) Customer guidance: please adopt the following short-term client-side practices to reduce amplification during pool warmup: exponential backoff with jitter (start 200ms), limit aggressive retry loops for scoring endpoints during the next 7 days while we add telemetry.

We appreciate your partnership and will follow up with the postmortem link and the support ticket INC-2029-4782. If you’d like a 30-minute walkthrough of the RCA with our engineers, I can schedule one early next week.

Best regards,
